title: Keep each TypeScript function at or below 50 code lines

facts.note: Non-test source files; test files and vendored/build directories are outside the scan.
Excluding test files and vendored/build directories.
Requires bun_ts_metrics_detector to count code lines per function body across the whole scan scope, including pre-existing functions (not only changed ones).

fires: Any non-test .ts/.tsx function in the scan scope whose body has more than 50 non-blank, non-comment lines, whether newly written or pre-existing.
bun_ts_metrics_detector reports COMPLEXITY-LENGTH-TS-001 for a function.
A perfectly linear function (cyclomatic complexity 1) of more than 50 sequential code lines.
doesNotFire: A function whose body exceeds 50 physical lines only because of blank lines and comment lines, with at most 50 code lines.
A function with exactly 50 code lines.
Functions in vendored or build output directories.

given: A non-test TypeScript/TSX function in the scanned source tree
when: its body is written, changed, or scanned
then: The function has at most 50 code lines (blank and comment lines excluded).
prefer: Diagnose first: the distinct responsibilities, stages, or invariants the function manages.
Find semantic seams (internal_seam): blocks nameable by one intention-revealing name, often introduced by a comment that becomes the helper's name.
Identify the data each candidate responsibility needs.
Extract one cohesive responsibility at a time.
Name helpers after their purpose, not their mechanics.
Keep related state and decisions together.
Leave the original as a readable top-level flow.
avoid: Splitting at an arbitrary line boundary, or moving contiguous lines elsewhere, just to get under 50.
Moving a long or complex block unchanged into another function.
A generalized abstraction unrelated to the extracted responsibility.
why: A function longer than a screen cannot be read as one unit, so its invariants are reconstructed from memory each time; length catches linear functions doing several unnamed things that complexity misses. The threshold is a sensor for weak cohesion or multiple responsibilities, not the objective — moving lines only removes the signal.
evidence: bun_ts_metrics_detector no longer reports COMPLEXITY-LENGTH-TS-001 for the triggering function.
Extracted functions satisfy the applicable complexity and nesting conventions.

Reviewer judges that resulting names and boundaries make the responsibilities easier to understand (a successful refactor identifies a responsibility or cohesive operation that deserves its own name and boundary).
The refactor introduces no new ATDD Bun violations.
verifier_detail: Threshold: a function fails when its code-line count is > 50 (at most 50 allowed). Applies to every TypeScript/TSX function in scope.
code_line: a line inside the function body that is neither blank nor a comment; blank lines and comment lines are not counted.

Counts non-blank, non-comment lines between the function's signature and its matching closing brace, found by a string- and comment-aware brace matcher so a `}` inside a string never closes a body early (counting invariant; it does not suppress real findings).
Scope: TypeScript/TSX functions; test files and vendored/build directories are outside the scan.

Length is the crudest of the three per-function metrics and the hardest to argue with; it catches a different fault from cyclomatic complexity (e.g. fifty sequential assignments score complexity 1 yet may do five things that wanted names).
Finding alias: COMPLEXITY-LENGTH-TS-001; detector ref: bun_ts_metrics_detector (type validator).
